exactBefore.scenario: ANALYZE 50,003 same-install activity rows plus movement ties and identities, then insert 50,003 newer unrelated activity rows without refreshing statistics. Original equality predicate and time-only ordering scan the global time index.

fixedDiagnostics.after: Custom and generic plans on PG15/17 keep the installation key through singleton ANY plus full key ordering. Exact uses the existing3key index; movement uses its type-literal partial3key indexes.

regressions: Scalar exact equality let PostgreSQL drop the installation ordering key and filter50003 newer unrelated rows through the global time index after natural statistics lag.
A movement stream reproduced the same50003-row global-time-index overread when old statistics described one all-applied installation.
Singleton array predicates plus complete3key order retain native installation indexes under custom and forced generic plans without planner GUCs or removal of the global index.
Blocking session advisory lock before CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY deadlocked on its own old snapshot; fail-fast try-lock makes one contender visibly busy and permits explicit retry.
Two type-specific partial3key indexes preserve the old index-key width instead of adding a type key that can reject a formerly admitted long identity.
Empty, escaped, long Unicode, case/NFC distinct and astral installation IDs preserve identity; NUL/lone surrogate PostgreSQL queries perform no lossy driver replacement.
Future and equal-cutoff events committed after observing the DB clock stay excluded; activity-only installations remain discoverable through exact latest lookup.
Dropped, wrong-predicate, mixed-order, mismatched or nondeterministic collation indexes fail before raw reads.

limits: Exact lookup remains internal; movement pages remain behind the prototype event-page path until the required provider/HTTP/RPC/Console cutover.
Live all-installation enumeration and its full-domain JS ordering remain unresolved and unimplemented.
PostgreSQL index preparation is explicit. Incomplete owned indexes require deliberate repair; concurrent preparation fails busy rather than automatically waiting/retrying.
Mongo committed source is an unimplemented reviewed plan only. Every other-provider source/report/search engine and public port remains unfinished.
Legacy50000-row runtime, optional eventPages and v1 prototype still await direct replacement; this slice adds no compatibility approval.
No raw event deletion, rewrite, retention limit or new installation-ID length restriction.
Plans measure these fixtures on cached PostgreSQL15/17; they do not guarantee planner choice, byte memory, billing, disk I/O or throughput for arbitrary data.
Sequential standalone E2E remains pending complete implementation and20GiB disk readiness; current free space is below that threshold.
